newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Airlines says not hedging fuel.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Airlines says not hedging fuel.

text.p: Malaysian Airline Systems Bhd (MAS) officials confirmed to Reuters on Friday that the national carrier would not be hedging fuel prices.

Malaysian press reports quoted MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli as saying on Thursday the airline would not currently be hedging fuel prices, as it was only involved in doing so on certain routes and during the northern winter season.
"Fuel-hedging is a very expensive exercise and we do not do it completely. Very few companies are involved in hedging," said Ramli.
Fuel costs make up around 10 percent of the airline's total operating cost, said Tajudin.
MAS officials did not give details on the extent of hedging by the airline.
MAS said on Thursday that it had submitted a proposal to the Malaysian government to raise its international air fares by three percent, citing rising jet fuel prices as the main reason.
The government had earlier announced that it was agreeable to a price rise on international routes, as the government only controlled domestic fares.
